events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.74 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
RydeTAXI trip, one off-route segment F3 (09:47–09:53, 3.83 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.89 km, +1.94 km), so RD-1 is engaged and the segment must be reviewed against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5. The metre-based fare is affected by extra distance, so RD-2's meter branch (amount = Σ non-exempt extra_km × distance_fare ÷ distance_km) governs [F3][F4][F6][RD-1][RD-2].

RD-4 is settled against the driver: the trace shows no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, and the two speed-band facts (F10, F11) are band 4 on AYE and Kent Ridge Road, neither of which is band 1–2, and in any case band evidence alone does not exempt [F10][F11][F12][RD-4].

RD-3 does not exempt the segment. The only rider message is the 09:35 kerb/locator message at Mandarin Gallery, a pick-up arrangement before the trip; the record measures no stop in the segment, and the driver's own statement says he followed his GPS reroute, not a rider-named stop [F7][F9][RD-3].

RD-5 also fails to exempt. The chat record is complete (1 message, all timestamped) and contains no rider agreement to any route, chatted or in-app, before the segment began at 09:47:50; the kerb message is neither a general route choice nor a specific named road, and the driver's claim that his GPS rerouted him is a statement, not rider consent [F3][F7][F8][F9][RD-5][G11]. The trace's evidence question asks for a RHR — nothing in the fact table ties this segment to anywhere the rider did not agree to, so the segment counts as an unexempted detour.

Amount: the fare record gives this trip's rate as distance fare ÷ distance km = $18.50 ÷ 13.12 km = $1.410061/km; the segment's extra distance is 3.83 km − 1.89 km = 1.94 km; 1.94 km × $1.410061/km = $2.7355 → $2.74. (The billed excess line F4 uses $1.4101 and 2.44 km = $3.44, i.e. the whole trip's excess, inclusive of the ~0.3 km remainder not attributed to any segment; RD-2 refunds only the unexempt segment, so $2.74, not $3.44) [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 1 prior dispute upheld but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, and the case count alone never decides the case — no flag_account [F15][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.74 Ryde voucher to the rider under NS-7 for the non-exempt detour mileage (voucher form, no cash); no account flag — no prior upheld route dispute on the driver's record.

We reviewed a route dispute on one of your RydeTAXI trips. Outcome: the off-route portion is not exempt, so the rider receives a partial refund of $2.74 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: the trip went 3.83 km where the best route covers 1.89 km, and nothing on the record exempts that stretch — the rider gave no route agreement for it, and band or GPS evidence alone does not exempt a detour.
